question: When our company's data protection officer does their job, do they have to pay more attention to the riskier ways we handle people's information?
If a company has posted my personal information online and has to delete it because I asked, does it also have to tell other websites that copied or linked to it that I want it removed?
Where can I find an official list of countries that have been approved, or no longer approved, as having good enough data protection for sending personal information abroad?
Can the European body that coordinates data protection regulators be told what to do by outside parties like governments or companies when it carries out its work?
Does a small partnership or club that regularly earns money count as a business under the data protection rules, even if it isn't a formal company?
If I agree to let a company use my personal details, can I change my mind later, and should stopping be just as simple as signing up?
Does the data protection regulator in my country have to keep its own log of companies that broke the privacy rules and what penalties or corrective steps it imposed on them?
Can an organization use my sensitive details, like health or religion information, without my consent if it's done for an important public benefit that a law allows and protects me?
What does a company have to prove before it is allowed to hand out data protection certificates or seals to other businesses?
If a data protection authority in another country asks for help with my case, can they use the information they receive for anything other than the reason they asked for it?
What does it mean when the data protection rules talk about an online service, and where can I find the official description of that term?
Does the national data protection authority in my country give advice to the government and lawmakers when they are drafting new rules that affect people's privacy?
If I hire an outside company to handle my customers' data, what must our agreement say about the company only acting on my written instructions, including sending data abroad?
If I send a saliva sample to a DNA testing company, does the information about my body and health that they get from it count as a special kind of personal data?
Can my employer handle sensitive details about me, like health information, if it's needed to meet job-related legal duties such as sick pay or social security rules?
If a court in a non-EU country orders my company to hand over customer data, do we have to comply right away?

If my company shares personal data between its branches in different countries under internal company rules, how must those rules explain to people how they will be told about their rights and protections, beyond the usual privacy notices?
If a company wants to use the information it collected from me for a new reason I never agreed to, what should it think about to decide whether the new use is still acceptable?
If a company I hired to handle data starts deciding for itself why and how to use that data, does it become responsible like the owner of the data?
Can our church or club keep records about our members' beliefs without asking each person's permission, as long as we don't share the information with anyone outside the group?
Can the data protection authority in my country take a company that broke privacy rules to court?
If our company's internal data-sharing rules for international transfers get updated, how do we have to keep track of the changes and let the data protection regulator know?
What counts as a global organization, like a group created by an agreement between several countries, when it comes to handling my personal data?
If a data protection authority leading a cross-border case agrees with another country's regulator who objected to its proposed decision, what happens next and how quickly do they have to respond?
Who decides what the little standardised pictures that explain how my data is used should show, and how companies should provide them?
If I hire an outside company to handle my customers' data, does our contract have to say they'll help me meet my security, breach-reporting, and risk-assessment duties?

If national data protection regulators disagree about my company's case and it goes to the EU-level group of regulators for review, can any of them issue their own ruling while that review is still going on?
If the European data protection authorities can't reach a decision on a cross-border dispute in time, how is the final decision made, and who breaks the tie if the vote is evenly split?
What basic rules does a company have to follow when it collects, uses, stores, and protects my personal information?
If a privacy regulator in one EU country thinks people's data needs protecting right away, can it skip the usual slow process of working with the main regulator on a case?
When can a data protection regulator in one EU country turn down another country's regulator who asks for help with a privacy case?
If the EU approved a country's data protection standards under the old privacy law from before 2018, is that approval still valid today?
What are the internal company data protection policies that let a business group send personal information to its branches or partner companies in countries outside the EU?
If I hire an outside company to handle my customers' information, does our contract have to say they'll help me answer people who ask to see or fix their data?
If my company is based outside Europe, who is the person or business we have to appoint in writing to act for us on our data protection duties inside the EU?
If a company operates in several EU countries and is investigated over a data problem, do the different national privacy regulators have to work together and share what they know?
If a company gets my details from somewhere other than me, what else do they have to tell me, like how long they'll keep my data and where they got it?

If a new law already required a general risk review before it was passed, does my public agency still have to do its own separate privacy risk check before starting the data handling that the law sets out?
If my information is sent to a company in another country, can I ask what protections are in place to keep it safe?
Can I file a complaint about how my personal data was handled using an online form, or do I have to send a letter?
Can a company charge me money or turn me down if I keep asking to see the personal data they hold about me?
If my complaint about a company is turned down, which data protection office tells me the outcome and does the company also get told?
Can my small business choose to appoint someone to handle data privacy compliance even if the rules don't strictly force us to?

If a company I run is being investigated over a data problem, can the main privacy regulator ask regulators in other EU countries for help or team up with them to check on a business based in another country?
If a company lets a computer make an important decision about me automatically, what can I ask for to make sure a real person looks at it and I can argue against the result?
Can a healthcare provider handle my sensitive health information for my treatment if the staff member involved is legally bound to keep patient details confidential?
If a data protection regulator in another country asks our country's regulator for help with a case, how quickly does it have to respond?

If a data protection regulator in one country isn't doing enough to stop a problem that urgently threatens people's privacy, can another country's regulator ask the European-level board to step in quickly?
As a small business that handles customer data, what must I do to show I'm following the privacy rules, and do I need to keep revisiting those steps as things change?
Where can I find a public list of approved data protection certifications and seals, and the standards a certifying organization has to meet?
